title: Getting Started with randomPlantedForest
text: see model recovers, simulate data true components known. outcome depends x1, x2 x3 main effects different shapes x1 x2 jointly product interaction x4 effect : y=1+sin⁡(πx1)+2(x22−13)+x32+2x1x2+εy = 1 + \sin(\pi x_1) + 2\left(x_2^2 - \tfrac{1}{3}\right) + \tfrac{x_3}{2} + 2 x_1 x_2 + \varepsilon uniform predictors [−1,1][-1, 1], term mean zero interaction main-effect part, terms exactly components model meant estimate. max_interaction = 2 restricts forest main effects two-way interactions. central tuning choice method: lower values give interpretable, constrained model, max_interaction = 0 allows interactions order. ntrees sets number tree families ensemble. Prediction works usual: Note rpf() handle missing values: rows containing NA must imputed removed beforehand (see recipes section one way part model specification).
code: set.seed(1) n <- 1000 sim <- data.frame(   x1 = runif(n, -1, 1),   x2 = runif(n, -1, 1),   x3 = runif(n, -1, 1),   x4 = runif(n, -1, 1) ) true_effects <- list(   x1 = function(x) sin(pi * x),   x2 = function(x) 2 * (x^2 - 1 / 3),   x3 = function(x) x / 2 ) sim$y <- 1 +   true_effects$x1(sim$x1) +   true_effects$x2(sim$x2) +   true_effects$x3(sim$x3) +   2 * sim$x1 * sim$x2 +   rnorm(n, sd = 0.3) rpfit <- rpf(y ~ ., data = sim, max_interaction = 2, ntrees = 50) rpfit #> ── Regression Random Planted Forest ──────────────────────────────────────────── #> Formula: `y ~ .` #> 50 tree families with 30 splits each on 4 predictors, interactions to degree 2. #> ℹ Forest is not purified. #>  #> ── Tree growing  #>    split_structure: leaves #>          split_try: 10 #>              t_try: 0.4 #>     max_candidates: 50 #>   split_decay_rate: 0.1 #>      delete_leaves: TRUE #>  #> ℹ Fit using 1 thread, also the default for `predict()` and `purify()`. predict(rpfit, new_data = head(sim)) #> # A tibble: 6 × 1 #>     .pred #>     <dbl> #> 1 -0.217  #> 2  0.0562 #> 3  1.27   #> 4  3.83   #> 5  1.17   #> 6  0.955

title: Getting Started with randomPlantedForest
text: interaction order bounded, prediction function sum low-dimensional components: m̂(x)=m̂0+∑km̂k(xk)+∑k<lm̂kl(xk,xl)\hat{m}(x) = \hat{m}_0 + \sum_k \hat{m}_k(x_k) + \sum_{k < l} \hat{m}_{kl}(x_k, x_l) predict_components() returns exactly decomposition: intercept one column per main effect interaction term, evaluated supplied data. forest purified internally make decomposition unique, print method reports purification state. components sum exactly model prediction: column components$m isolated contribution one predictor (one pair) prediction, scale outcome. standard deviations give simple importance measure: three main effects x1:x2 interaction dominate, x4 interactions close zero, . estimated main effects follow true functions (blue lines). tree-based model, flatten towards edges data, observations available determine .  interaction function two variables, shown heatmap. evaluate estimated x1:x2 component grid. Note x3 x4 must present new data affect component.  plots drawn manually predict_components() illustration. glex package provides ggplot2 versions : glex() computes decomposition fitted rpf object, plot_main_effect() plot_twoway_effects() draw main effects two-way interactions.
code: components <- predict_components(rpfit, new_data = sim)  components$intercept #> [1] 0.9862177 names(components$m) #>  [1] "x1"    "x2"    "x3"    "x4"    "x1:x2" "x1:x3" "x1:x4" "x2:x3" "x2:x4" #> [10] "x3:x4" pred_sum <- components$intercept + rowSums(components$m) pred_direct <- predict(rpfit, new_data = sim)$.pred  all.equal(pred_sum, pred_direct) #> [1] TRUE round(sort(sapply(components$m, sd), decreasing = TRUE), 3) #> x1:x2    x1    x2    x3 x2:x3 x1:x3    x4 x1:x4 x2:x4 x3:x4  #> 0.656 0.655 0.573 0.258 0.026 0.007 0.000 0.000 0.000 0.000 op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1)) for (v in names(true_effects)) {   ylim <- range(components$m[[v]], true_effects[[v]](sim[[v]]))   plot(     sim[[v]],     components$m[[v]],     pch = 20,     col = "darkgray",     ylim = ylim,     xlab = v,     ylab = "component"   )   curve(true_effects[[v]](x), add = TRUE, lwd = 2, col = "blue") } par(op) grid_points <- seq(-1, 1, length.out = 50) grid <- expand.grid(x1 = grid_points, x2 = grid_points, x3 = 0, x4 = 0) estimated <- predict_components(rpfit, new_data = grid, predictors = c("x1", "x2"))$m[["x1:x2"]]  surfaces <- list(   true = outer(grid_points, grid_points, function(x1, x2) 2 * x1 * x2),   estimated = matrix(estimated, nrow = length(grid_points)) ) zlim <- c(-1, 1) * max(abs(unlist(surfaces)))  op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1)) for (s in names(surfaces)) {   image(     grid_points,     grid_points,     surfaces[[s]],     zlim = zlim,     col = hcl.colors(51, "Blue-Red 3"),     xlab = "x1",     ylab = "x2",     main = paste(s, "x1:x2")   ) } par(op)

code: penguins <- na.omit(palmerpenguins::penguins)  rpfit_sex <- rpf(sex ~ ., data = penguins, ntrees = 50)  predict(rpfit_sex, head(penguins), type = "prob") #> # A tibble: 6 × 2 #>   .pred_female .pred_male #>          <dbl>      <dbl> #> 1       0.0591    0.941   #> 2       0.806     0.194   #> 3       0.995     0.00546 #> 4       0.998     0.00219 #> 5       0.0243    0.976   #> 6       0.992     0.00801 predict(rpfit_sex, head(penguins), type = "class") #> # A tibble: 6 × 1 #>   .pred_class #>   <fct>       #> 1 male        #> 2 female      #> 3 female      #> 4 female      #> 5 male        #> 6 female

title: Getting Started with randomPlantedForest
text: Multiclass classification works way: probability predictions contain one column per class: default loss classification "exponential", gives proper probability estimates. "logit" gives similar results slower, "L1" "L2" fit class indicators directly yield proper probabilities. Note loss = "logit", multiclass models fit reference-class (log-odds) scale, link predictions components one column less classes: see ?predict.rpf details.

code: library(recipes)  # rows with a missing outcome still need to be dropped by hand peng_raw <- subset(palmerpenguins::penguins, !is.na(body_mass_g))  rec <- recipe(body_mass_g ~ ., data = peng_raw) |>   step_impute_median(all_numeric_predictors()) |>   step_impute_mode(all_nominal_predictors())  rpfit_rec <- rpf(rec, data = peng_raw, ntrees = 50)  predict(rpfit_rec, head(peng_raw)) #> # A tibble: 6 × 1 #>   .pred #>   <dbl> #> 1 3801. #> 2 3491. #> 3 3572. #> 4 3482. #> 5 4006. #> 6 3422.

text: rpf object holds forest external pointer C++ object, saveRDS() preserve, meaning naively saved restored model usable: Use rpf_marshal() convert model plain R list saving, rpf_unmarshal() loading: Alternatively, bundle method wrapping mechanism available via bundle::bundle() bundle::unbundle().
code: tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds") saveRDS(rpfit, tmp) broken <- readRDS(tmp)  rpf_is_valid(broken) #> [1] FALSE predict(broken, head(sim)) #> Error in `predict()`: #> ! The C++ forest behind this <rpf> object is gone. #> ℹ Most likely it was saved with `saveRDS()` and restored with `readRDS()`. #> ℹ Use `blob <- rpf_marshal(x)` before saving and `rpf_unmarshal(blob)` after #>   loading, see `?rpf_marshal()`. saveRDS(rpf_marshal(rpfit), tmp) restored <- rpf_unmarshal(readRDS(tmp))  all.equal(   predict(restored, head(sim)),   predict(rpfit, head(sim)) ) #> [1] TRUE

what: Random Planted Forest: A Directly Interpretable Tree Ensemble
title: Random Planted Forest: A Directly Interpretable Tree Ensemble
text: randomPlantedForest implements Random Planted Forest (Hiabu, Mammen & Meyer), tree ensemble whose predictions can read directly, without post-hoc explanation methods. Like random forest, averages many tree-based models grown bootstrap samples. Unlike random forest, models sum trees split fixed set predictors, max_interaction bounds many predictors can . max_interaction = 1 forest additive model; 2 adds pairwise interactions, . result, fitted model decomposes exactly intercept, main effects interactions order: m̂(x)=m̂0+∑km̂k(xk)+∑k<lm̂kl(xk,xl)+…\hat m(x) = \hat m_0 + \sum_k \hat m_k(x_k) + \sum_{k < l} \hat m_{kl}(x_k, x_l) + \dots component can inspected plotted , together sum prediction.

title: Random Planted Forest: A Directly Interpretable Tree Ensemble
text: rpf() takes formula, x/y data recipe, predict() returns tibble tidymodels: predict_components() returns decomposition: one column per main effect interaction, plus intercept. glex package plots components:  Get started guide covers classification, recipes, saving models interpreting components, Bikesharing decomposition article works larger example.
code: library(randomPlantedForest)  mtcars$cyl <- factor(mtcars$cyl) rpfit <- rpf(mpg ~ cyl + wt + hp, data = mtcars, ntrees = 25, max_interaction = 2) rpfit #> ── Regression Random Planted Forest ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #> Formula: `mpg ~ cyl + wt + hp` #> 25 tree families with 30 splits each on 3 predictors, interactions to degree 2. #> ℹ Forest is not purified. #>  #> ── Tree growing  #>    split_structure: leaves #>          split_try: 10 #>              t_try: 0.4 #>     max_candidates: 50 #>   split_decay_rate: 0.1 #>      delete_leaves: TRUE #>  #> ℹ Fit using 1 thread, also the default for `predict()` and `purify()`.  head(predict(rpfit, new_data = mtcars)) #> # A tibble: 6 × 1 #>   .pred #>   <dbl> #> 1  21.4 #> 2  21.0 #> 3  24.4 #> 4  20.9 #> 5  17.7 #> 6  19.1 components <- predict_components(rpfit, new_data = mtcars) head(components$m) #>          cyl         wt         hp     cyl:wt      cyl:hp        hp:wt #>        <num>      <num>      <num>      <num>       <num>        <num> #> 1: 2.8275105  0.2569457  0.2970626  0.3448129  0.06873138  0.006002504 #> 2: 2.8275105 -0.2438784  0.2970626  0.3929089  0.06873138  0.076817727 #> 3: 4.8022694  1.7754646  1.3572422 -0.4610986 -0.41379471 -0.231709254 #> 4: 2.8275105 -0.4727413  0.2970626  0.3538112  0.06873138  0.256989969 #> 5: 0.7661282 -1.0143147 -0.3952336  0.4528133  0.02336632  0.241715900 #> 6: 2.8275105 -1.1525180  0.5397470 -0.4590129 -0.03247695 -0.199217461 library(glex) library(ggplot2) library(patchwork)  (autoplot(components, "wt") + autoplot(components, "hp")) /   (autoplot(components, "cyl") + autoplot(components, c("wt", "hp")))

code: fit <- rpf(mpg ~ wt + cyl, data = mtcars, ntrees = 10) blob <- rpf_marshal(fit) tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds") saveRDS(blob, tmp) restored <- rpf_unmarshal(readRDS(tmp)) all.equal(predict(fit, mtcars), predict(restored, mtcars)) #> [1] TRUE

title: randomPlantedForest 0.5.0
text: rpf() now defaults max_interaction = 2, main effects pairwise interactions, instead 1, additive model (#66). Values number predictors capped silently instead message. rpf() now defaults loss = "exponential" classification instead "L2", classification fits give proper probability estimates default; regression still uses "L2" (#66). rpf() arguments reordered purpose (forest size, split search, loss, ). Pass arguments data arguments name (#66). rpf(), predict() purify() error unknown arguments, misspelled ones, instead silently ignoring (#66). purify() regular function instead S3 generic (#66). preprocess_predictors_predict() longer exported; internal step predict() (#66). package now requires R >= 4.1.0 (#66). given seed, classification models differ 0.4.0 due fixes speedup , regression models unchanged (#57, #66). direct users C++ object ($fit): set_data() longer fits, call fit() afterwards, unknown classification loss error instead silent fallback L2 (@jyliuu, #57). rpf() longer cv argument, never effect: C++ cross-validation -op (#66).

title: randomPlantedForest 0.5.0

Previously rows silently received arbitrary predictions, rpf() handling missing values. rpf() likewise reports missing values training data column (#66). Classification fits fixed seed differ runs. split replaced leaf, new split candidates lost attached wrong leaf, depending memory layout (#66). predict(type = "class") breaks probability ties level order instead random, class predictions deterministic longer advance random number generator (#66). purify() returns input invisibly, documented (#66). Logical predictors formula interface used single 0/1 column, x/y interface. Previously expanded two redundant indicator columns, also counted max_interaction (#66).

Classification fits slightly faster, redundant work model construction removed (#57).

title: randomPlantedForest 0.3.0
text: split_structure = "leaves": Defines split candidate candidates drawn. One "leaves" (default), "hist", "cur_trees_1", "cur_trees_2", "res_trees"; see ?rpf details. max_candidates = 50: Maximum number split candidates sampled per iteration. split_decay_rate = 0.1: Exponential aging repeatedly drawn unchosen split candidates. split_decay_rate = 0 corresponds aging uniform sampling. delete_leaves = TRUE: Whether parent leaf deleted splitting along existing dimension. Fitting results change: new candidate-sampling defaults reworked internal RNG mean fits reproducible previous versions, even seed. Install older commit exact reproduction previous results required. Seeded fits now reproducible regardless nthreads: per-tree seeds drawn R’s RNG, set.seed() gives identical forests serial multithreaded fits. Substantial speedups fitting (cached per-leaf orderings, prefix sums) reduced memory use (training-buffers released tree family built). mode = 2: Purification algorithm; 2 new fast exact method, 1 legacy grid-based path. nthreads = NULL: Purification now multithreaded, defaulting fit’s nthreads setting. maxp_interaction = NULL: Optionally compute purified components interaction order. New rpf() argument export_forest = FALSE: flattened forest longer stored fitted object default, rpf_object$forest NULL unless export_forest = TRUE. reduces object size; predict(), purify(), predict_components() unaffected. preprocess_predictors_predict() now exported. Fixed memory bug legacy purification path grid sized one element large, causing --bounds reads (crashes Windows, silently wrong purification results elsewhere). Fixed crash Windows fitting nthreads > 1, caused thread_local buffer non-trivial destructor destroyed thread exit.
